page: Microsoft Azure E32ps_v6 is an ARM-based virtual machine belonging to the Epsv6 server family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 32 dedicated physical cores powered by the Microsoft Neoverse-N2 processor architecture operating at 3.4 GHz, with a single thread per core. The hardware configuration includes 256.0 GB of RAM, providing a memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or integrated GPUs, though it is Premium Storage capable for external disk attachments.

In benchmark evaluations, the E32ps_v6 demonstrates top-tier memory performance, achieving a PassMark memory score in the top 10% and uncached large-block read and write memory bandwidths of 436.06 GB/sec and 184.19 GB/sec respectively. Multi-core CPU performance is strong, with a Geekbench multi-core score of 19664.0 and a stress-ng multi-core score of 66283.59. However, single-core performance is average, as evidenced by a Geekbench single-core score of 1661.0. Large-scale LLM prompt processing is a notable bottleneck, scoring in the bottom 10% with 4.66 tokens/sec for a 70B model, though smaller model inference remains average.

The server offers high qualitative cost efficiency for memory-intensive workloads due to its high resource density and top-tier database operation performance. The dedicated ARM cores provide predictable execution without hyperthreading overhead. This profile makes the E32ps_v6 highly suitable for relational databases, caching layers, multi-threaded compilation, and static web serving, while it is less optimal for single-threaded tasks or large-scale AI model inference.
